name: Muscular system
description: The skeletal muscles and how they work: muscle tissue, how muscles move the bones, and the main muscles of the head and neck, the trunk, the arm and the leg, with their attachments and actions. Picture questions show the body with one muscle highlighted to name.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: Roughly how many skeletal muscles are in the human body?
questions.explanation: Counts vary between about 600 and 650, depending on how muscles with several parts are counted. They make up 35 to 40% of body weight.

figure.alt: The muscles of the whole body from the front
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which type of muscle tissue is striated and under voluntary control?
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle moves the skeleton. It is striped (striated) under the microscope because its filaments line up in sarcomeres.

questions.prompt: Which type of muscle tissue is striated but involuntary, with its cells joined by intercalated discs?
questions.explanation: Found only in the heart. Intercalated discs carry gap junctions, so each beat spreads from cell to cell.

questions.prompt: Which type of muscle tissue lines the walls of hollow organs and blood vessels and has no striations?
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle works slowly and without conscious control: it moves food along the gut, narrows blood vessels and empties the bladder.

questions.prompt: What is a single skeletal muscle cell called?
questions.explanation: Long and thin with many nuclei, because it forms when many embryonic cells (myoblasts) fuse. One fibre can run the length of a muscle.

questions.prompt: What is a bundle of muscle fibres, wrapped in perimysium, called?
questions.explanation: Muscle is bundles of bundles: myofibrils inside fibres, fibres inside fascicles, fascicles inside the whole muscle.

questions.prompt: What is the layer of connective tissue around a whole muscle called?
questions.explanation: Epi- (upon) the muscle. Perimysium wraps each fascicle and endomysium each fibre; all three run together into the tendon.

questions.prompt: What is the thin layer of connective tissue around each muscle fibre called?
questions.explanation: Endo- means within. The sarcolemma is the fibre's own cell membrane, just inside it.

questions.prompt: What are the long rod-like bundles of filaments that fill a muscle fibre called?
questions.explanation: Each myofibril is a chain of sarcomeres, end to end.

questions.prompt: What is the repeating contractile unit of a myofibril, from one Z disc to the next?
questions.explanation: When a muscle contracts, every sarcomere along its fibres shortens a little.

questions.prompt: Which protein makes up the thick filaments of a sarcomere?
questions.explanation: Myosin heads reach out to grab the thin filaments and pull, using energy from ATP.

questions.prompt: Which protein makes up most of the thin filaments of a sarcomere?
questions.explanation: Thin filaments also carry tropomyosin and troponin, which cover the binding sites until calcium arrives.

questions.prompt: What is the theory that a muscle shortens because its thin filaments slide past its thick ones, called?
questions.explanation: The filaments themselves stay the same length; they overlap more, so each sarcomere gets shorter.

questions.prompt: Which ion, released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, lets a muscle fibre contract?
questions.explanation: Calcium binds to troponin, which moves tropomyosin off actin's binding sites so myosin can grab hold. Pumping it back relaxes the fibre.

questions.prompt: Which neurotransmitter does a motor neuron release onto a skeletal muscle fibre?
questions.explanation: It is released at the neuromuscular junction. Curare and some nerve agents work by blocking it or stopping its breakdown.

questions.prompt: What is the junction between a motor neuron and a muscle fibre called?
What is one motor neuron and all the muscle fibres it supplies called?
questions.explanation: Muscles for fine control (around the eye) have small motor units of a few fibres; big postural muscles have units of over a thousand.

questions.prompt: What must bind to myosin for it to let go of actin?
questions.explanation: Without fresh ATP the heads stay locked on. That is why muscles stiffen after death (rigor mortis).

questions.prompt: Which red protein stores oxygen inside muscle fibres?
questions.explanation: Slow-twitch fibres are full of it, which is why they look red.

questions.prompt: Which muscle fibres are red, full of mitochondria and resist fatigue, suiting long steady work?
questions.explanation: Postural muscles like the soleus are mostly slow-twitch; sprinters have more fast-twitch (type II) fibres, which tire quickly.

questions.prompt: What is the cord of dense connective tissue that joins a muscle to a bone called?
questions.explanation: Ligaments join bone to bone. Tendons are mostly collagen, so they barely stretch and pass the pull straight on.

questions.prompt: What is a broad, flat sheet of tendon called?
questions.explanation: Examples: the aponeurosis on top of the skull between frontalis and occipitalis, and those of the abdominal muscles, which meet at the linea alba.

questions.prompt: What is the growth of a muscle from training, by its fibres getting bigger, called?
questions.explanation: Adults make few new muscle fibres; existing ones add myofibrils. Disuse does the opposite: atrophy.

questions.prompt: What is the attachment of a muscle that stays fixed while it contracts (usually the one nearer the trunk) called?
questions.explanation: A muscle pulls its insertion towards its origin.

questions.prompt: What is the attachment of a muscle on the bone it moves called?
What is the muscle mainly responsible for a movement called?
questions.explanation: The biceps brachii and brachialis are agonists for bending the elbow.

questions.prompt: What is a muscle that opposes a movement, relaxing to let it happen, called?
questions.explanation: The triceps is the antagonist of the biceps. Muscles can only pull, so every movement needs one to undo it.

questions.prompt: What is a muscle that helps the prime mover, or cancels out an unwanted movement it makes, called?
What is a muscle that holds the origin of the prime mover steady called?
questions.explanation: For example, muscles holding the scapula still so the deltoid can lift the arm.

questions.prompt: What is a contraction in which the muscle shortens as it pulls called?
questions.explanation: Lifting a cup is concentric for the biceps.

questions.prompt: What is a contraction in which the muscle lengthens while still pulling (lowering a weight slowly) called?
questions.explanation: Walking downhill works the quadriceps eccentrically. These contractions cause most of the soreness the next day.

questions.prompt: What is a contraction in which the muscle pulls but does not change length called?
questions.explanation: Holding a plank, or pushing against a wall. Iso- (same) -metric (length).

questions.prompt: In muscle names, what do maximus, medius and minimus describe?
questions.explanation: As in the gluteus maximus, medius and minimus. Longus and brevis (long and short) and major and minor work the same way.

questions.prompt: In muscle names, what do biceps, triceps and quadriceps describe?
questions.explanation: Two, three and four heads (separate origins) joining one tendon.

questions.prompt: What does rectus mean in a muscle's name, as in rectus abdominis?
questions.explanation: Its fibres run straight, parallel to the body's midline. Oblique and transversus name the other directions.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The front belly of the occipitofrontalis, over the forehead. It raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead.

figure.alt: The face, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The ring of muscle around the eye. Its thin inner part blinks; the outer part screws the eye shut.

figure.alt: The face, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle closes the eyelids?
questions.explanation: Levator palpebrae superioris opens the upper lid. Orbicularis oculi is supplied by the facial nerve, so in Bell's palsy the eye can't close.

figure.alt: The face, with the orbicularis oculi in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The ring of muscle in the lips. It closes and purses the mouth, as in whistling or a kiss.

figure.alt: The face, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the cheekbone (zygomatic bone) to the corner of the mouth.

figure.alt: The face, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle pulls the corner of the mouth up and out in a smile?
questions.explanation: Depressor anguli oris does the opposite, turning the corners of the mouth down.

figure.alt: The face, with the zygomaticus major in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The muscle of the cheek, deep to the masseter (taken away here).

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which cheek muscle keeps food between the teeth while chewing, and blows air out as when playing a trumpet?
questions.explanation: Bucca is Latin for cheek; buccinator means trumpeter. It is a muscle of facial expression, not of chewing.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the buccinator in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression?
questions.explanation: When it fails on one side (Bell's palsy), that half of the face droops. The chewing muscles are supplied by the trigeminal nerve instead.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The thick muscle over the angle of the jaw, from the zygomatic arch to the ramus of the mandible.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which thick muscle over the angle of the jaw bulges when you clench your teeth?
questions.explanation: It raises the mandible to close the jaw. For its size it is one of the strongest muscles in the body.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the masseter in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A fan over the side of the skull (the scalp muscles are taken away here). Its tendon passes under the zygomatic arch to the coronoid process of the mandible.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The temporalis inserts on the coronoid process of the mandible. What does it do?
answers: Closes the jaw and pulls it back
wrong: Moves the jaw side to side only
questions.explanation: Its front fibres lift the mandible; its back fibres, running almost horizontally, pull it backwards. Feel it work at your temple as you bite.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the temporalis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which pair of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Deep to the ramus of the mandible, from the pterygoid plates of the sphenoid. The skull is drawn without the other muscles here.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The muscles of mastication are the masseter, the temporalis and which other two?
questions.explanation: All four are supplied by the mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve.

questions.prompt: Which muscle of mastication opens the jaw, by pulling the head of the mandible forward?
questions.explanation: The other three close the jaw. The lateral pterygoid also moves it from side to side when grinding food.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the pterygoid muscles in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the sternum (sterno-) and clavicle (cleido-) to the mastoid process behind the ear.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: When the left sternocleidomastoid contracts on its own, which way does the face turn?
questions.explanation: It pulls the mastoid process (behind the left ear) towards the sternum, which turns the face to the other side and tilts the head towards the same shoulder. Both together bend the neck forward.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the left sternocleidomastoid in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: A baby's head tilts to one side with the chin turned away because one neck muscle is short and tight. Which muscle?
questions.explanation: Congenital torticollis (wry neck). Gentle stretching usually fixes it.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A thin sheet in the skin of the neck, from the upper chest to the jaw.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which thin sheet of muscle in the skin of the neck tightens the skin and pulls the corners of the mouth down?
questions.explanation: It is a muscle of facial expression, supplied by the facial nerve. It stands out as cords in the neck during a grimace.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the platysma in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Two bellies: the back one from the mastoid notch, the front one to the chin, joined by a tendon slung to the hyoid.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle under the jaw has two bellies joined by a tendon held to the hyoid bone?
questions.explanation: Di- (two) gastric (belly). It lowers the mandible and raises the hyoid in swallowing. The omohyoid also has two bellies, but runs down to the scapula.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the digastric in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Anterior, middle and posterior scalenes, from the cervical vertebrae down to the first and second ribs. The sternocleidomastoid and trapezius are taken away here.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which neck muscles raise the first two ribs during deep breathing, with the brachial plexus passing between two of them?
questions.explanation: The brachial plexus and subclavian artery pass between the anterior and middle scalenes.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the scalenes in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Deep to the trapezius (taken away here), from the lower neck vertebrae up to the mastoid process and the occipital bone.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle under the trapezius extends the head and turns the face to its own side?
questions.explanation: It works with the opposite sternocleidomastoid to turn the head.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the splenius capitis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Sternohyoid, sternothyroid, thyrohyoid and omohyoid, below the hyoid bone.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What do the infrahyoid (strap) muscles do?
answers: Lower the hyoid bone and larynx
Pull down the hyoid and larynx
questions.explanation: They bring the larynx back down after swallowing. The suprahyoid muscles (digastric, mylohyoid and others) raise it.

figure.alt: The head and neck, with the infrahyoid muscles in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead in surprise?
questions.explanation: Corrugator supercilii pulls the eyebrows together into a frown.

figure.alt: The face, with the frontalis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle closes and purses the lips?

figure.alt: The face, with the orbicularis oris in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The big fan of the chest, from the clavicle, sternum and costal cartilages to the humerus.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What does the pectoralis major do to the arm?
answers: Pulls it across the chest and turns it in
questions.explanation: Its clavicular part also lifts the arm forward (flexes it). Push-ups and the bench press work it.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with the pectoralis major in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Under the pectoralis major (taken away here), from the 3rd to 5th ribs to the coracoid process.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The pectoralis minor runs from the ribs to which part of the scapula?
questions.explanation: It pulls the scapula forward and down against the chest wall.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with the pectoralis minor in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Saw-toothed (serrated) slips from the upper eight or nine ribs, wrapping round to the inner edge of the scapula.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle holds the scapula against the chest wall and pulls it forward, as in a punch?
questions.explanation: Sometimes called the boxer's muscle.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with the serratus anterior in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Damage to the long thoracic nerve makes the scapula stick out from the back (a winged scapula). Which muscle has stopped working?
questions.explanation: The nerve runs on the side of the chest wall, where it can be hurt in surgery or by a heavy load on the shoulder.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A small muscle under the clavicle, from the first rib. It steadies the clavicle.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the pubis to the 5th to 7th costal cartilages and the xiphoid process.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle forms the 'six-pack', divided into sections by tendinous intersections?
questions.explanation: It bends the trunk forward (as in a sit-up) and is held in a sheath formed by the aponeuroses of the other three abdominal muscles.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with the rectus abdominis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the fibrous band down the midline of the abdomen, where the abdominal aponeuroses meet, called?
questions.explanation: Latin for white line. It runs from the xiphoid process to the pubic symphysis, between the two recti.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The outermost flat muscle of the side of the abdomen.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which abdominal muscle has fibres running down and forward, like hands in your front pockets?
questions.explanation: The internal oblique, under it, runs at right angles to it. The lower edge of the external oblique's aponeurosis forms the inguinal ligament.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with the external oblique in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The middle layer of the side of the abdomen (the external oblique is taken away here). Its fibres fan up and forward.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The deepest flat muscle of the abdomen (both obliques and the rectus are taken away here).

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which deepest abdominal muscle, with horizontal fibres, wraps round like a corset to squeeze the abdomen?
questions.explanation: It squeezes the abdomen when coughing, straining and breathing out hard, and helps steady the lower back.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with the transversus abdominis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: From outside in, what are the three flat muscles of the side of the abdomen?
answers: External oblique, internal oblique, transversus abdominis
wrong: Internal oblique, external oblique, transversus abdominis
Transversus abdominis, internal oblique, external oblique
External oblique, transversus abdominis, internal oblique
questions.explanation: Each layer's fibres run in a different direction, like plywood.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The dome between the chest and the abdomen, seen through the ribs.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the main muscle of breathing in?
questions.explanation: When it contracts the dome flattens and moves down, enlarging the chest so air flows in.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with the diaphragm in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: From the neck, spinal nerves C3, 4 and 5: "C3, 4 and 5 keep the diaphragm alive". A high neck injury can stop breathing.

questions.prompt: Which large vessel passes through the diaphragm at the level of the 8th thoracic vertebra?
questions.explanation: Inferior vena cava at T8, oesophagus at T10 and aorta at T12 ("I 8 10 eggs at 12").

questions.prompt: Which muscles are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The muscles between the ribs (the chest and abdominal muscles are taken away here).

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles between the ribs raise the ribcage when you breathe in?
questions.explanation: Their fibres run the same way as the external oblique's. The internal intercostals, at right angles to them, pull the ribs down in forced breathing out.

figure.alt: The trunk from the front, with the external intercostals in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A large diamond over the upper back and neck, from the skull and the spines of the vertebrae to the clavicle and scapula. The two together make a trapezium.

figure.alt: The back, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle shrugs the shoulders?
questions.explanation: Its upper fibres lift the scapula (with the levator scapulae), its middle fibres pull it back and its lower fibres pull it down. Upper and lower together rotate it so the arm can go overhead.

figure.alt: The back, with the trapezius in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which cranial nerve supplies the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid?
questions.explanation: Testing a shrug and turning the head against a hand checks it.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The broadest muscle of the back, from the lower spine and the iliac crest to the front of the humerus.

figure.alt: The back, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which broad back muscle pulls the arm down and back, as in a pull-up or a swimming stroke?
questions.explanation: It extends, adducts and medially rotates the arm. It inserts in the intertubercular groove of the humerus, with the teres major.

figure.alt: The back, with the latissimus dorsi in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Rhomboid major and minor, under the trapezius (taken away here), from the spine to the inner edge of the scapula.

figure.alt: The back, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles between the spine and the scapula pull the shoulder blades together?
questions.explanation: They retract the scapula, working against the serratus anterior. Middle trapezius helps.

figure.alt: The back, with the rhomboids in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the upper four neck vertebrae to the upper corner of the scapula, under the trapezius.

figure.alt: The back, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What does the levator scapulae do?
questions.explanation: As its name says: levator (lifter) of the scapula. Its tightness is a common cause of a stiff neck.

figure.alt: The back, with the levator scapulae in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Three columns either side of the spine, under the other back muscles (taken away here).

figure.alt: The back, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The erector spinae has three columns. From outside in, what are they?
questions.explanation: "I Love Spine" (or spaghetti), from lateral to medial. Together they straighten and arch the back.

figure.alt: The back, with the erector spinae in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A square (quadratus) muscle of the loin (lumborum), from the iliac crest to the 12th rib and the lumbar vertebrae.

figure.alt: The pelvis, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which square muscle of the lower back bends the trunk to the side and holds the 12th rib down?
questions.explanation: It also hitches the hip up on one side, and is a common source of low back pain.

figure.alt: The pelvis, with the quadratus lumborum in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Psoas major from the lumbar vertebrae and iliacus from the inside of the ilium, joining to one tendon.

figure.alt: The pelvis, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is the strongest flexor of the hip, inserting on the lesser trochanter of the femur?
questions.explanation: It lifts the thigh in walking and running and pulls the trunk up in a sit-up.

figure.alt: The pelvis, with the iliopsoas in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The pelvis from above: the levator ani (pubococcygeus, puborectalis and iliococcygeus) and the coccygeus.

figure.alt: The pelvis, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the main muscle of the pelvic floor, a sling holding up the pelvic organs, called?
questions.explanation: Made of pubococcygeus, puborectalis and iliococcygeus. Puborectalis loops round the rectum and helps keep it closed.

figure.alt: The pelvis, with the pelvic floor in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The rounded muscle over the shoulder, from the clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula to the deltoid tuberosity on the humerus.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle lifts the arm out to the side (abduction) once the movement has started?
questions.explanation: Supraspinatus starts the movement for the first 15 degrees or so, then the deltoid takes over. Its front fibres also flex the arm and its back fibres extend it.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with the deltoid in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The deltoid is named after its shape. What is it shaped like?
questions.explanation: An upside-down Greek delta. It is a common place for injections.

questions.prompt: A dislocated shoulder or a broken neck of the humerus can damage which nerve, weakening the deltoid?
questions.explanation: It winds round the surgical neck of the humerus. It also supplies the teres minor and a patch of skin over the deltoid.

questions.prompt: Which four muscles make up the rotator cuff?
answers: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis
wrong: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres major and subscapularis
Deltoid, supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor
Supraspinatus, teres major, teres minor and subscapularis
questions.explanation: SITS. Their tendons blend with the shoulder joint's capsule and hold the head of the humerus in the shallow glenoid. Teres major is not one of them.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with the rotator cuff muscles in red

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Above the spine of the scapula (the trapezius and deltoid are taken away here), its tendon passing under the acromion to the greater tubercle.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which rotator cuff tendon is torn most often?
questions.explanation: Its tendon is squeezed under the acromion when the arm is raised (impingement). It starts abduction of the arm.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with the supraspinatus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Below the spine of the scapula, to the greater tubercle of the humerus.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which two rotator cuff muscles rotate the arm outwards (laterally)?
questions.explanation: Both lie on the back of the scapula and insert on the greater tubercle, behind the supraspinatus.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with the infraspinatus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A small muscle along the outer edge of the scapula, just below the infraspinatus. It is part of the rotator cuff.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the lower corner of the scapula to the front of the humerus, beside the latissimus dorsi. It is not part of the rotator cuff.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle from the lower corner of the scapula helps the latissimus dorsi to adduct and medially rotate the arm, and is not part of the rotator cuff?
questions.explanation: Sometimes called "lat's little helper".

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with the teres major in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: On the front of the scapula, facing the ribs (drawn here without the ribcage and other muscles), to the lesser tubercle of the humerus.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which rotator cuff muscle rotates the arm inwards (medially)?
questions.explanation: The only one on the front of the scapula and the only one on the lesser tubercle.

figure.alt: The right shoulder, with the subscapularis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Two heads, from the coracoid process and from above the glenoid, to the radial tuberosity.

figure.alt: The right arm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Besides bending the elbow, what strong movement of the forearm does the biceps brachii make?
questions.explanation: It inserts on the radius, so it rolls the radius over, turning the palm up, like turning a screwdriver clockwise with the right hand.

figure.alt: The right arm, with the biceps brachii in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The tendon of the long head of the biceps runs in which groove of the humerus?
questions.explanation: Between the greater and lesser tubercles, then inside the shoulder joint to the top of the glenoid.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Under the biceps (taken away here), from the front of the humerus to the ulna.

figure.alt: The right arm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is the main flexor of the elbow, whether the palm faces up or down, because it pulls on the ulna?
questions.explanation: The ulna can't rotate, so the brachialis flexes the elbow in any position: the workhorse of elbow flexion.

figure.alt: The right arm, with the brachialis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the coracoid process to the middle of the humerus, on the inner side of the arm.

figure.alt: The right arm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The muscle on the back of the arm, with long, lateral and medial heads, to the olecranon of the ulna.

figure.alt: The back of the right arm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle straightens (extends) the elbow?
questions.explanation: It inserts on the olecranon. Its long head starts on the scapula, so it also helps to pull the arm back.

figure.alt: The back of the right arm, with the triceps brachii in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the three heads of the triceps brachii?
questions.explanation: The biceps has a long and a short head; the triceps a long, a lateral and a medial one.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A small triangle from the lateral epicondyle to the olecranon. It helps the triceps extend the elbow.

figure.alt: The back of the right arm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From above the lateral epicondyle of the humerus down to the styloid process of the radius.

figure.alt: The right arm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which forearm muscle bends the elbow most strongly with the thumb pointing up, as when lifting a mug or hammering?
questions.explanation: It runs from the humerus (brachio-) to the radius, and stands out on the forearm when you bend your elbow against resistance.

figure.alt: The right arm, with the brachioradialis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Tennis elbow is pain where the wrist extensors start. Where is that?
questions.explanation: The common extensor origin, mostly from the extensor carpi radialis brevis. Golfer's elbow is at the medial epicondyle, where the flexors start.

questions.prompt: Most muscles on the front of the forearm start from which bony point?
questions.explanation: The common flexor origin. The extensors on the back start from the lateral epicondyle.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the medial epicondyle diagonally across to the middle of the radius. The forearm is drawn palm forward.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which two muscles turn the palm down (pronate the forearm)?
wrong: Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
questions.explanation: Pronator quadratus does most of the work; pronator teres helps when it is fast or against resistance.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with the pronator teres in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A square muscle across the lower ends of the radius and ulna, under all the flexor tendons. Drawn here without the other muscles.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Wrapped round the top of the radius, from the lateral epicondyle and the ulna. Drawn here without the other muscles.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which two muscles turn the palm up (supinate the forearm)?
questions.explanation: Supination is stronger than pronation, mostly thanks to the biceps. That is why screws tighten clockwise, to suit right-handed people.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with the supinator in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the medial epicondyle to the bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals, on the thumb side.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A thin muscle with a long tendon into the palm, in the middle of the front of the forearm.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which forearm muscle is missing in about one person in seven, and is often used for tendon grafts?
questions.explanation: Press your thumb and little finger together and bend the wrist: if you have one, its tendon stands out in the middle of the wrist.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with the palmaris longus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: On the little finger side of the forearm, to the pisiform, hamate and 5th metacarpal.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which carpal bone is a sesamoid bone in the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris?
questions.explanation: Flexor carpi ulnaris bends the wrist and tilts it towards the little finger (ulnar deviation).

figure.alt: The right forearm, with the flexor carpi ulnaris in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The middle layer of the front of the forearm (the outer muscles are taken away here). Its four tendons go to the middle phalanges.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The deep layer, from the ulna. Its four tendons go to the distal phalanges.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle bends the fingertips (the joint nearest the nail)?
questions.explanation: Profundus reaches the distal phalanges by passing through a split in each superficialis tendon, which stops at the middle phalanges: "S splits in two to let P pass through".

figure.alt: The right forearm, with the flexor digitorum profundus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Flexor digitorum superficialis inserts on the middle phalanges. Which finger joints can it bend on its own?
questions.explanation: Hold the other fingers straight and bend one finger: the middle joint bends but the tip stays loose. That tests superficialis.

figure.alt: The right forearm, with the flexor digitorum superficialis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The finger flexor tendons and which nerve pass through the carpal tunnel?
questions.explanation: Swelling in the tunnel squeezes the nerve: tingling in the thumb and first fingers, and in time wasting of the thenar muscles.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the lateral epicondyle down the middle of the back of the forearm, to the four fingers.

figure.alt: The back of the right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle on the back of the forearm straightens the four fingers?
questions.explanation: Its tendons spread into an extensor hood over each finger. The index and little fingers have an extra extensor each, so they can point on their own.

figure.alt: The back of the right forearm, with the extensor digitorum in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles are highlighted in red?
answers: Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
questions.explanation: Two muscles on the thumb side of the back of the forearm, to the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals. They extend the wrist and tilt it towards the thumb.

figure.alt: The back of the right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: On the little finger side of the back of the forearm, to the 5th metacarpal. It extends the wrist and tilts it towards the little finger.

figure.alt: The back of the right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles are highlighted in red?
answers: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis and longus
wrong: Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
Extensor indicis and extensor digiti minimi
questions.explanation: The deep muscles of the thumb, coming out from between the other extensors: abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis and extensor pollicis longus.

figure.alt: The back of the right forearm, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The hollow at the base of the thumb when it is stretched out (the anatomical snuffbox) lies between the tendons of extensor pollicis longus and which others?
answers: Extensor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis longus
Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
wrong: Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
questions.explanation: The scaphoid lies in its floor, so tenderness there after a fall suggests a broken scaphoid.

figure.alt: The back of the right forearm, with the deep thumb muscles in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis and opponens pollicis, forming the ball of the thumb.

figure.alt: The right hand, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle brings the thumb across the palm to touch the fingertips?
questions.explanation: Opposition is what lets us grip and pinch. Opponens pollicis is one of the thenar muscles, supplied by the median nerve.

figure.alt: The right hand, with the thenar muscles in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Abductor, flexor and opponens digiti minimi, forming the mound on the little finger side of the palm.

figure.alt: The right hand, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Four small worm-shaped (lumbricus is Latin for earthworm) muscles in the palm, starting from the tendons of flexor digitorum profundus.

figure.alt: The right hand, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which small muscles bend the knuckles while straightening the finger joints, as when holding a card?
questions.explanation: They pull on the extensor hood from the palm side of the knuckle. The interossei help.

figure.alt: The right hand, with the lumbricals in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Four muscles between the metacarpals, seen from the back of the hand.

figure.alt: The right hand, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The palmar interossei adduct the fingers and the dorsal interossei abduct them. What is the memory aid?
questions.explanation: Palmar ADduct, Dorsal ABduct, measured from the middle finger. Both are supplied by the ulnar nerve.

figure.alt: The right hand, with the dorsal interossei in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The big muscle of the buttock, from the back of the ilium, sacrum and coccyx to the femur and the iliotibial tract.

figure.alt: The hips from behind, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle extends the hip powerfully, as in climbing stairs or standing up from a chair?
questions.explanation: The largest muscle in the body by mass. It does little in level walking but a lot in climbing, running and jumping.

figure.alt: The hips from behind, with the gluteus maximus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Under the gluteus maximus (taken away here), from the outer ilium to the greater trochanter.

figure.alt: The hips from behind, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: When standing on one leg, the pelvis drops on the other side. Which muscles on the standing side are weak?
questions.explanation: A positive Trendelenburg sign. Gluteus medius and minimus abduct the hip and keep the pelvis level with every step.

figure.alt: The hips from behind, with the gluteus medius in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The deepest of the three, under the gluteus medius, to the front of the greater trochanter.

figure.alt: The hips from behind, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Pear-shaped, from the front of the sacrum out through the greater sciatic notch to the greater trochanter.

figure.alt: The hips from behind, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle in the buttock does the sciatic nerve usually leave the pelvis just below?
questions.explanation: Piriformis is the landmark of the buttock. It rotates the hip outwards (laterally), as do the small muscles below it.

figure.alt: The hips from behind, with the piriformis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A small muscle at the front of the hip, from the iliac crest into the iliotibial tract.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which structure is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A thick band of fascia down the outside of the thigh to the tibia, pulled on by the tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus. The leg is seen from its outer side.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What is the thick band of fascia down the outside of the thigh, from the hip to the tibia, called?
questions.explanation: It steadies the hip and knee. Runners can get pain where it rubs over the outside of the knee.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the iliotibial tract in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A long strap running diagonally across the front of the thigh, from the anterior superior iliac spine to the inside of the tibia.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which is the longest muscle in the body?
questions.explanation: The tailor's muscle: it flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip and bends the knee, the movements of sitting cross-legged.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the sartorius in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which three muscles' tendons join on the inside of the tibia, at the pes anserinus (goose's foot)?
questions.explanation: "Say Grace before Tea": Sartorius, Gracilis, semiTendinosus, one from each compartment of the thigh.

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Four muscles at the front of the thigh joining one tendon round the patella.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which four muscles make up the quadriceps femoris?
answers: Rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis and vastus intermedius
wrong: Rectus femoris, sartorius, vastus lateralis and vastus medialis
Vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, gracilis and rectus femoris
Biceps femoris, rectus femoris, vastus lateralis and vastus medialis
questions.explanation: They extend the knee, pulling through the patella and the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the quadriceps in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The straight muscle down the middle of the front of the thigh, from the anterior inferior iliac spine.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part of the quadriceps also flexes the hip, because it starts on the pelvis?
questions.explanation: The three vasti start on the femur and cross only the knee. Rectus femoris crosses the hip too, so it is used hard in kicking.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the rectus femoris in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The largest part of the quadriceps, down the outside of the thigh.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The teardrop on the inside of the thigh just above the knee.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part of the quadriceps forms the teardrop above the inside of the knee and keeps the patella from sliding outwards?
questions.explanation: Its lowest fibres pull the patella inwards, against the outward pull of the rest of the quadriceps.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the vastus medialis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Under the rectus femoris (taken away here), lying on the front of the femur.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: From the pubis to the middle of the femur. Its outer edge borders the femoral triangle.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles on the inside of the thigh pulls the legs together, and is hurt in a groin strain?
questions.explanation: Adductor longus, brevis and magnus, with gracilis and pectineus. Most are supplied by the obturator nerve.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the adductor longus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The biggest adductor, from the pubis and ischial tuberosity to most of the length of the femur. Seen here from behind.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A long, slender (gracilis) strap down the inside of the thigh, from the pubis to the tibia. It is the only adductor that crosses the knee.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A short flat muscle at the top of the inner thigh, from the pubis to below the lesser trochanter.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which group of muscles is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Biceps femoris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus, on the back of the thigh.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What two movements do the hamstrings make?
answers: Bend the knee and extend the hip
Flex the knee and extend the hip
wrong: Straighten the knee and flex the hip
Bend the knee and flex the hip
questions.explanation: They start on the ischial tuberosity (the bone you sit on) and cross both joints. A sprinter's pulled hamstring is usually in the biceps femoris.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with the hamstrings in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The outer hamstring, with a long head from the ischial tuberosity and a short head from the femur, to the head of the fibula.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which part of the hamstrings does not cross the hip?
questions.explanation: It starts on the femur (the linea aspera), so it only bends the knee.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with the biceps femoris in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The inner hamstring with the long rope-like tendon (half tendon), on top of the semimembranosus.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The inner hamstring with the flat, membrane-like tendon at its top, under the semitendinosus.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The two-headed calf muscle, from the back of the femur above the knee to the calcaneus.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which two muscles join to form the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon?
questions.explanation: Together they are called triceps surae (the three heads of the calf). They point the foot down (plantarflexion), as in rising on tiptoe.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with the gastrocnemius in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The flat muscle under the gastrocnemius (taken away here), from the tibia and fibula. Shaped like a sole fish.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which calf muscle can point the foot down just as well with the knee bent, because it doesn't cross the knee?
questions.explanation: Gastrocnemius starts above the knee, so it is slack when the knee is bent. Soleus, mostly slow-twitch fibres, keeps us from swaying forward when standing, and squeezes blood back up the leg veins.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with the soleus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which tendon is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The tendon of the calf muscles, to the back of the calcaneus.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which is the thickest and strongest tendon in the body?
questions.explanation: It can bear several times body weight when running. A sudden tear feels like a kick in the back of the ankle.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with the calcaneal tendon in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A small muscle with a very long thin tendon, between the gastrocnemius (taken away here) and soleus. Missing in about one person in ten.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: A small muscle in the back of the knee, from the lateral femur to the back of the tibia (the calf muscles and hamstrings are taken away here).

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which small muscle at the back of the knee 'unlocks' the straightened knee so it can bend?
questions.explanation: When the knee is fully straight it is locked by a slight twist; popliteus untwists it.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with the popliteus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The deepest calf muscle, between the tibia and fibula, its tendon passing behind the medial malleolus into the sole. Drawn here without the other muscles.

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which deep calf muscle turns the sole inwards and holds up the medial arch of the foot?
questions.explanation: When its tendon fails, the arch slowly falls (adult acquired flatfoot).

figure.alt: The back of the right leg, with the tibialis posterior in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Beside the shin, from the tibia to the medial cuneiform and the first metatarsal.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle lifts the foot (dorsiflexion) and turns the sole inwards, so that if it is paralysed the foot drops and the toes catch when walking?
questions.explanation: Foot drop is often from injury to the common fibular nerve where it winds round the neck of the fibula.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the tibialis anterior in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: On the front of the leg, outside the tibialis anterior, with four tendons to the lesser toes.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Between the tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus, with its tendon to the big toe (hallux).

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle lifts the big toe?
questions.explanation: Hallux is the big toe; hallucis means 'of the big toe'. Flexor hallucis longus, at the back, bends it down.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the extensor hallucis longus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Down the outside of the leg from the head of the fibula. The leg is seen from its outer side.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscles on the outside of the leg turn the sole outwards (eversion)?
wrong: Extensor digitorum longus and extensor hallucis longus
questions.explanation: Their tendons pass behind the lateral malleolus. Formerly called the peroneal muscles.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the fibularis longus in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Under the fibularis longus (taken away here), to the base of the 5th metatarsal.

figure.alt: The right leg, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: The tendon of which muscle crosses the sole of the foot to the base of the first metatarsal, helping to support the arches?
questions.explanation: With the tibialis anterior on the inside, it forms a stirrup under the foot.

questions.prompt: A twisted ankle can pull off the bone where which tendon inserts, on the base of the 5th metatarsal?
questions.explanation: An avulsion fracture of the 5th metatarsal, common in a rolled ankle.

figure.alt: The right leg, with the fibularis brevis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Along the inner edge of the sole, from the calcaneus to the big toe. The foot is seen from the inside.

figure.alt: The right foot, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which muscle is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: The middle of the first layer of the sole, from the calcaneus to the four lesser toes. The foot is seen from below.

figure.alt: The right foot, with one muscle in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: In how many layers are the muscles of the sole of the foot usually described?
questions.explanation: Abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis and abductor digiti minimi form the first, outermost layer.

figure.alt: The right foot, with the flexor digitorum brevis in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science
